visual.general_description: Two grayscale whole-body skeletal scintigraphy images (anterior view on the left, posterior view on the right) of one person, showing the skeleton as dark tracer uptake on a white background with a few focal dark foci.
visual.detailed_description: One image file holds two unlettered side-by-side grayscale planar bone-scan images separated by a thin vertical dark-gray line; dark pixels mean higher tracer uptake. The left image is an anterior projection (skull with orbits and facial bones, shoulders, sternum/ribs, pelvis and both legs) and the right image is a posterior projection (skull, vertebral column, scapulae, ribs, pelvis and both legs); the projection is judged from the anatomy shown, as no view label is printed. Uptake in the skull vault, shoulders, knees and ankles is generally prominent on both views. On the anterior view a single small intense focus lies at the level of one elbow on the image-left arm, and a large rounded dark area at the pelvic midline is the most intense structure. On the posterior view a cluster of small dark foci lies over the ribs of the image-right upper-to-mid thorax near the scapula, there are paired dark foci near the sacroiliac/posterior pelvic region, and slightly increased uptake appears at elbows and wrists. Both knees and both ankles show bilateral dark uptake on both views. No text, side marker (L/R), scale, date, name or identifier is visible, and the face is not photographically identifiable (scintigraphic outline only).

A few tiny curvilinear radiopaque marks lie within the pelvic cavity on the image-right side, and the lower border shows a soft-tissue/air shadow of the perineal region. No patient name, date, accession number or other burned-in identifier is visible, and no face is shown. The anatomy is the pelvis/hips and not the shoulders or right knee named in the caption.

visual.general_description: Coronal fat-suppressed MRI of both knees with R and inferior markers and a series/image overlay, showing patchy increased marrow signal.
visual.detailed_description: A single black-background coronal MR image pair, one knee on each half, showing the distal femur, joint line and proximal tibia of both knees with the surrounding soft tissues. Both knees show diffuse heterogeneous intermediate-to-high marrow signal in the distal femoral and proximal tibial marrow, brighter and more extensive on the tibial side, with a thin bright joint-line signal; small bright vessels and fascial lines appear in the soft tissue. No name, date or other identifying text is burned in.
